Decision brief

Atlas is ready for a staged launch to the first six design partners. The remaining gates are operational rather than architectural: customer support rotation, the final export-control review, and a documented rollback rehearsal.

The release is intentionally bounded. New tenants receive a stable ingestion contract, role-based views, auditable annotations, and a small set of integrations. Advanced anomaly training remains behind an experiment flag.

Decision requested: approve the 2026-09-14 controlled rollout, with a 48-hour hold after each cohort.

02 · Market and product storyNorthstar Atlas
Why now

From alert volume to operating clarity

Modern service teams do not lack telemetry; they lack a shared shape for interpreting it. Logs, traces, tickets, and ownership data arrive in different languages, leaving incident commanders to assemble a temporary narrative under pressure.

Atlas turns those fragments into a reviewable operating picture. A signal can be connected to a service, a service to a team, and a decision to the evidence that justified it. The product is useful when the room is busy because the context is already attached.

“The value is not another graph. It is the five minutes we get back when everyone sees the same graph and the same next action.”

— Pilot participant, platform reliability lead

Observe

Normalize events into a compact service timeline with provenance, severity, and retention controls.

Core

Explain

Attach deploys, ownership, runbooks, and annotations directly to the evidence under review.

Core

Coordinate

Give incident roles a shared handoff board without forcing every participant into the same workflow.

Pilot

Learn

Turn the final timeline into a durable review record and a small set of measurable follow-ups.

Later

Positioning principle

Atlas is a coordination surface, not a replacement for source-of-truth monitoring systems. It links evidence and decisions while leaving collection and alert evaluation with the systems that already own them.

Risk boundary: Atlas must never imply that an unavailable integration has produced a clean result. Empty, delayed, and disconnected states are shown distinctly in the product and in the export.

Audience and adoption signals

Platform leads. They want a service map that reflects how teams actually operate, including temporary ownership during an incident. Their strongest request was a fast path from a symptom to the responsible runbook.

Incident commanders. They value a narrow, printable summary at the end of a shift. The summary needs a timeline, decisions, unresolved questions, and explicit owners, not a screenshot wall.

Engineering managers. They need recurring patterns without turning every review into a performance ranking. Atlas separates learning signals from individual blame and keeps the evidence visible.

Adoption hypothesis. Teams will retain the workflow when the first useful view appears within one minute, the first annotation takes fewer than three clicks, and exports can be shared without granting broad workspace access.

04 · Architecture appendixNorthstar Atlas
Technical shape

Small contracts, observable boundaries

Collect

Adapters accept signed events and attach source, region, and arrival metadata.

Boundary: ingestion API

Shape

The normalizer maps source-specific fields into the Atlas event vocabulary.

Boundary: event model

Present

Views query a time-bounded projection and show missing context honestly.

Boundary: read model

Reference event contract

{
  "event_id": "evt_7f2a",
  "source": "deployments",
  "service": "checkout-api",
  "observed_at": "2026-08-18T14:20:00Z",
  "state": "degraded",
  "evidence": ["trace:8ab1", "deploy:331"],
  "visibility": "workspace"
}

Failure modes and responses

ConditionShown to userAction
Connector deniedAccess requiredRe-authorize source
Source delayedLast update + ageCheck connector health
Projection staleStale bannerPause automated decision
No matching evidenceNo evidence foundBroaden time window

Implementation checklist

  • Bound every query by tenant and region.
  • Keep source timestamps separate from arrival time.
  • Render unavailable integrations as a first-class state.
  • Preserve evidence order in print and JSON exports.
  • Emit correlation IDs in support diagnostics.

Deployment topology

Print note: the architecture appendix is designed to remain legible in monochrome; state labels carry meaning in text as well as color.

Design constraint: the read model may be eventually consistent, but it may not silently become authoritative. Every export carries its freshness timestamp and source coverage summary.

05 · Release decision recordNorthstar Atlas
Close the loop

Controlled rollout authorization

The steering group authorizes a controlled rollout to six design partners beginning 2026-09-14. The launch office will review cohort health after 48 hours and may expand, hold, or roll back based on the gates below.

Required launch actions

  1. Complete export redaction review and archive the fixture report.
  2. Run the support rotation rehearsal with the named escalation owner.
  3. Publish the customer-facing connector health glossary.
  4. Record cohort-one decision notes before enabling cohort two.

Decision options

OptionTriggerConsequence
ExpandAll green; no severe support eventsOpen next cohort
HoldAmber gate unresolved at reviewKeep cohort size stable
RollbackData isolation or stale-state breachDisable new writes
Current recommendation: expand after the two amber controls close. No coral stop condition is active.
